meta.title: Why we call the modern world Kafkaesque

beats.text: One morning you wake up — and you no longer belong in your own life.
Welcome to the world of Franz Kafka.
A man is arrested. No one will tell him the crime. The trial grinds on for years, through offices no one controls.
Another wakes transformed into an insect — and his family's only question is how to be rid of him.
Kafka isn't writing nightmares. He's writing the machine we live inside — the forms, the waiting rooms, the rules no one can explain.
Powerless. Unseen. Vaguely guilty of nothing at all.
He died almost unknown. Now his name is the word for it: Kafkaesque.

source_note: Ideas paraphrased (Kafka's English translations are in copyright) — no verbatim quotes.
